items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: He used to come on every Sunday and Lagraus would sing with him.

ctx.x: And was there church influence in the musical end of things for you?

I think so. I never went into the church and played piano in a church. That never happened. But my father loved to play saxophone. And so that certainly had to have some effect on me. Although he died when I was seven years old. But my sister played, my mother played, I had a brother who played the trumpet and violin, and I had another brother who played the saxophone and one who sang, actually two who sang. The oldest one sang but singing was never a major thing with him. He became a doctor. And the one next to…
Oh gee. I thought you were going to say finally they got me some lessons. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
